title: Ruling Chiefs of Hawaii (revised edition)
author: Samuel Mānaiakalani Kamakau
note: Translated from Kamakau's series in Ka Nupepa Kuokoa and Ke Au Okoa, 1866–1871 (first English edition 1961). The publisher states the book is free to read on Ulukau; Ulukau refused automated access, so it was read in the publisher's free PDF as re-hosted on the Internet Archive (item chiefs_202607). Page numbers are the 1992 edition's. Passages in square brackets are the editors' additions, not Kamakau's words.

title: An Account of the Polynesian Race, vol. II
author: Abraham Fornander
note: Public domain (London: Trübner). Read in full text with printed page numbers. Fornander counts thirty years to a generation, which puts his pre-contact dates earlier than later reckonings, and his theories of Polynesian origins are long superseded; his summaries of Hawaiian traditions and of the 1770s–1795 wars remain a main open source.

title: A Voyage to the Pacific Ocean, vol. II
author: James Cook
note: The official quarto edition. Book III, chapters XI–XII cover Kauaʻi and Niʻihau in January–February 1778; the end of the volume covers the approach to Kealakekua in January 1779.

title: A Voyage to the Pacific Ocean, vol. III
author: James King
note: King's continuation after Cook's death. Book V, chapters I–IV cover Kealakekua, January–February 1779; pp. 126–128 give his estimate of the islands' population.

title: History of the Sandwich Islands

author: Arthur Johnstone
note: In Thrum’s Hawaiian Almanac and Annual for 1908, pp. 160–167 (University of Michigan copy on the Internet Archive). title: Nuʻuanu, Oʻahu: A Native Place, Battle of Nuʻuanu

title: A Brief History of the Hawaiian People
author: W. D. Alexander
note: New York: American Book Company. Public domain; read in the Internet Archive full text for the reigns of Kamehameha IV and V and the election of Lunalilo (chs. XXXIV–XXXVI, pp. 280–299) and its chronological table. A history written for the kingdom’s schools by its Surveyor General.

title: Hawaiian Antiquities (Moolelo Hawaii)
author: David Malo, translated by N. B. Emerson
note: Bernice P. Bishop Museum Special Publication 2, Honolulu, 1903. Public domain; read in the Internet Archive full text for ch. XXXV, on war: the weapons the chiefs’ men practised with (§60, p. 257), the order of battle (§85, p. 260) and Emerson’s notes on each weapon (pp. 266–267).

title: The Great Mahele: Hawaii’s Land Division of 1848
author: Jon J. Chinen
note: University of Hawaii Press. On the Internet Archive in the LLMC collection, the author having waived his copyright for it. Read for the division of the lands into Crown, Government, Konohiki and kuleana lands and the acreage of each (p. 31).

title: Indices of Awards Made by the Board of Commissioners to Quiet Land Titles in the Hawaiian Islands
author: Office of the Commissioner of Public Lands, Territory of Hawaii
note: Honolulu: Star-Bulletin Press. Public domain; the Internet Archive scan (LLMC, from the Hawaii State Archives), read in its full text. Read: the Foreword; the Act of 7 June 1848 relating to the lands of the King and of the Government, which names the Crown and Government lands one by one (pp. 24–47); the Acts of 1890 on unassigned and unawarded lands (pp. 47–48); and, by machine over the text of both indices, the awards they mark as of a whole ahupuaʻa (“Ahp”). Its two-column scan loses names in places.

title: Buke Kakau Paa no ka Mahele Aina i Hooholoia iwaena o Kamehameha III a me na Lii a me na Konohiki ana
author: Kamehameha III and the chiefs
note: The Māhele Book of January–March 1848: the king’s and each chief’s quitclaims to one another, land by land, with the lists of Crown and Government lands on its last pages. The manuscript scan (LLMC, from the Hawaii State Archives) is open on the Internet Archive, but it is handwritten in Hawaiian and its machine text is unusable, so it was not read. Its page numbers are cited only as OHA’s Kīpuka layers give them.
wanted: Read by someone who reads the hand: each land's class and awardee as the book writes it, page by page, for mahele.json (its unknown units and its disputes first); and the lists of Crown and Government lands on the last pages, to check the crown and government classes.

title: Biennial Report of the Commissioners of Crown Lands, 1894
author: C. P. Iaukea, Agent of Crown Lands

Read: the report’s opening pages, on the Act of 3 January 1865 that made the Crown lands inalienable, and its table of the Crown lands by island (p. 8). OHA’s Crown lands layer cites its schedule of lands.

title: Crown_Lands_State (Crown and Government Lands), Kīpuka database
author: Office of Hawaiian Affairs
note: Queried in full on 2026-10-22: 219 tenure polygons, Crown (1848, 1890), Government (1848, 1850, 1853) and Konohiki, each with its Buke Māhele pages and, for a konohiki land, the chief the king relinquished it to and the award. It maps every land of Kauaʻi, Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi and Niʻihau and the Crown lands of the other islands, where its descriptions come from the 1894 Crown Lands report. A land the Buke Māhele divided between the king and a chief is drawn twice, the line between the halves unmapped. No licence is stated on the item.
